osint_summary:
**Public-mention summary (reviewed October 1, 2026):** Two distinct Bitcoin mainnet addresses match entries in the DOJ’s 2020 civil complaints. The complaint identifies **15K9…TNwpf** as Defendant Property 79 and alleges that Al Sadaqah solicited BTC donations to it on Telegram. ([justice.gov](https://www.justice.gov/d9/press-releases/attachments/2020/08/13/download_civil_complaints_.pdf)) It identifies **17QAW…P6MD** as Defendant Property 4 in a separate al-Qassam fundraising campaign; the supplied QR and human-review rows both refer to this same address and source, not two independent public mentions. ([justice.gov](https://www.justice.gov/d9/press-releases/attachments/2020/08/13/download_civil_complaints_.pdf))

These are allegations in civil complaints, not findings of fact. The supplied invalid and test-family rows are controls with unsupported attribution; they do not add public mainnet matches. This review makes no claim about address ownership, current control, or freeze status.
